resources.string: Buttocks seen from behind: the %1$s one split into 4 parts, upper outer part marked
Keep the button pressed, or part of the dose will leak
You can take the needle out
Inject slowly — less pain and fewer lumps
All in — you can take the needle out
As scheduled: %1$s. Only your doctor changes the dose
Next injection — %1$s. We will suggest the site that has rested longest.
This dose was already logged at %1$s. The app does not log it a second time — this guards against a double dose.
Wash your hands. The pen should be at room temperature: cold insulin stings more. Keep spare pens in the fridge, but not the one in use.
Look at the solution. If the leaflet says it is clear but it is cloudy, with flakes or crystals, do not inject — take a new pen.
A new one every time: a blunt needle hurts more and leaves lumps. Take off both caps and keep the big one — you will need it at the end.
Dial 2 U, hold the pen needle up, tap it and press the button all the way — a drop should appear at the needle tip. No drop — repeat, up to 3 times.
Turn the button to your dose and check the window.
%1$s. Not into scars, bruises or lumps; a finger’s width from the last injection.
%1$s. At least 5 cm from the navel, not into scars, bruises or lumps; a finger’s width from the last injection.
Abdomen — at least 5 cm from the navel; front and side of the thigh; buttock; back of the upper arm. Not into scars, bruises or lumps; a finger’s width from the last injection.
4 mm needle — straight in at 90°, no need to pinch the skin. A needle of 6 mm or longer, or little fat under the skin — pinch the skin. Press the button all the way and hold it during the countdown.
Take the needle out, put the big cap back on and unscrew the needle. Drop it into a hard container with a lid. Do not rub the site.
Wash your hands. On a clean napkin: the ampoule, a 5 ml syringe, two alcohol wipes, a needle container.
Name and dose match the prescription. There should be no sediment or flakes in the solution.
Wipe the ampoule neck and snap it away from you through a wipe. Draw %1$s, turn the syringe needle up, tap it and push the air out until the first drop.
%1$s. Split the buttock into 4 parts in your mind and inject into the upper outer part.
%1$s. Thigh — middle of the outer side.
Buttock — upper outer quarter; thigh — middle of the outer side; upper arm — 3 fingers below the shoulder bone.
Wipe the site with an alcohol wipe and wait until it dries — it stings less.
Stretch the skin with two fingers, put the needle in quickly at 90°, three quarters of its length. Inject slowly — about 10 seconds per 1 ml.
Take the needle out and press the site with a dry wipe. Do not recap the needle — straight into the container.
Repeat the test, up to 3 times. Still no drop — change the needle and test again. Still nothing — take another pen and do not use this one.
Leaked or the needle came out early
Do not inject again — you could get a double dose. We will log the injection as “leaked”. Check your sugar as your doctor advised; if unsure, call them.
Press with a dry wipe for a minute, do not rub. It happens and is not dangerous. Frequent bruises — show the sites to your doctor.
Sharp pain or numbness in the leg
Stop and take the needle out — a nerve may have been touched. Do not use this spot again and call your doctor.
Press with a dry wipe for a minute. It happens and is not dangerous. Frequent bruises — tell your doctor.
It usually goes away in a few days. If it gets redder, hurts more and more, or you get a fever — see a doctor.
This guide does not replace training: do your first injection with a nurse or doctor. The medicine leaflet and your doctor come first.
A reminder, not training: do your first injection with a nurse or doctor. The medicine leaflet and your doctor come first.
Needle, angle, sites, volume, when to see a doctor
Skin cross-section: a short needle at 90°, the medicine goes into the fat under the skin
A short needle at 90° — the medicine goes into the fat under the skin and is absorbed slowly and evenly.
Cross-section: a long needle at 90° passes the fat, the medicine goes into the muscle
A long needle at 90° passes the skin and fat — the medicine goes into the muscle and is absorbed faster.
4–6 mm for a pen, a new one every time.
90°. Pinch the skin only if the needle is 6 mm or longer, or there is little fat under the skin.
Abdomen — at least 5 cm from the navel; front and side of the thigh; buttock; back of the upper arm.
A new spot every time — a finger’s width from the last one; areas in turn. The app shows which one has rested.
Hold the pen button for 10 seconds, then take the needle out. Do not rub the site.
For the buttock — a 5 ml syringe: its needle is longer. A new needle every time.
90°, quickly, three quarters of the needle — not all the way to the hub.
Buttock — upper outer quarter; thigh — middle of the outer side; upper arm — 3 fingers below the shoulder bone.
Buttock and thigh — up to %1$s ml, upper arm — no more than %2$s ml.
Slowly — about 10 seconds per 1 ml: less pain and fewer lumps.
Right and left side in turn.
Wash your hands before the injection.
Not into scars, moles, bruises, lumps or inflamed skin.
Needles go into a hard container with a lid, not the trash bag.
Injection logged — no second one: the app stops a double dose.
A rash all over, swelling of the face or lips, trouble breathing.
The site gets redder, more swollen and more painful over a day or two; you get a fever; hard lumps appear at injection sites.
